recognize_zh: 骨髓抹片中一群成簇的大細胞，細胞核圓至橢圓、偏向一側，染色質細緻，細胞質豐富呈灰藍色、邊界模糊，部分細胞質內可見離核較遠的淡染區；這種成群排列、淡染區不緊貼核旁的特徵是造骨細胞（osteoblast），可與漿細胞區分。
features: Cohesive cluster of large cells (roughly 2-3 times the size of the adjacent small lymphocyte)
Round to oval, eccentrically placed nuclei with low N:C ratio
Finely granular, evenly distributed chromatin; nucleoli inconspicuous
Abundant gray-blue to basophilic cytoplasm with indistinct cell borders
Pale clear zone within the cytoplasm, separated from the nucleus
Background of dense blue-staining particle/stromal material
describe_en: Bone marrow aspirate smear shows a cohesive cluster of large cells with abundant, gray-blue cytoplasm and poorly defined cell borders. Nuclei are round to oval and eccentrically placed, with finely granular chromatin and inconspicuous nucleoli. Several cells show a pale cytoplasmic clear zone located away from the nuclear membrane. The cells lack the coarse clock-face chromatin and juxtanuclear hof of plasma cells, and there is no nuclear pleomorphism or mitotic activity to suggest a metastatic tumor. Findings are consistent with a cluster of osteoblasts.

ddx.vs: Plasma cells are smaller, occur singly rather than in cohesive sheets, have coarse clock-face chromatin, and their perinuclear hof lies immediately adjacent to the nucleus rather than at a distance from it.
Carcinoma clusters show nuclear pleomorphism, high N:C ratio, prominent nucleoli and nuclear molding, unlike the uniform bland nuclei of osteoblasts.
Osteoclasts are much larger multinucleated cells with many separate, uniform nuclei in a single cytoplasm, whereas osteoblasts are mononuclear cells grouped together.
Erythroid precursors have centrally placed round nuclei, deeply basophilic cytoplasm and a higher N:C ratio, and do not form cohesive sheets with indistinct borders.
